children: The brokerage assigns a Buy rating to ACME Solar and a Neutral rating to NTPC Green Energy, citing storage opportunities, project execution and transmission constraints

Nomura has picked ACME Solar Holdings as its preferred renewable energy play over NTPC Green Energy, betting on the growing value of battery storage and round-the-clock power supply as India scales up clean energy capacity.

The Japanese brokerage initiated coverage with a Buy rating and a target price of Rs 505 for ACME Solar, while assigning NTPC Green Energy a Neutral rating and a target price of Rs 100. The contrasting assessments highlight a growing divide in India’s clean energy market: developers are increasingly being evaluated not only on planned renewable capacity but also on their ability to commission projects, integrate storage and deliver electricity when demand peaks.

India’s renewable energy capacity has expanded rapidly, but intermittent solar and wind generation has created challenges for grid management. Surplus solar power during the day and higher electricity demand outside solar hours have strengthened the case for battery energy storage systems (BESS) and firm, dispatchable renewable energy projects. According to market reports, the share of grid-storage-backed tenders rose from 22 per cent in financial year 2021–22 to 87 per cent in 2025–26, underlining the increasing importance of storage in renewable energy procurement.
Storage Strengthens ACME Solar’s Growth Outlook

Nomura expects ACME Solar’s revenue to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 66 per cent and earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) at 65 per cent between FY27 and FY29. The brokerage expects the company to add 4.3 gigawatts (GW) of contracted capacity during the period. The company is transitioning from a conventional solar independent power producer to a platform offering firm and dispatchable renewable power. More than half of its portfolio capacity is linked to firm and dispatchable renewable energy projects, which combine generation with storage to meet specified electricity supply schedules.

ACME Solar’s total portfolio stood at around 8.4 GW, including a recently awarded 300 MW project. Of this, approximately 3 GW was operational, while projects under execution provided further growth potential. Falling battery costs and early commissioning of storage assets could also improve project economics. Bringing storage online ahead of scheduled project completion can allow developers to monetise electricity through merchant and short-term markets, while improving returns on invested equity.
Transmission Constraints Cloud NTPC Green’s Prospects

Nomura expects NTPC Green Energy’s revenue and EBITDA to grow at CAGRs of 74 per cent and 72 per cent, respectively, between FY27 and FY29. The projections are supported by planned capacity additions, an extensive project pipeline and the parent company NTPC’s execution experience and relatively low borrowing costs. NTPC Green has approximately 12.9 GW of capacity under construction through its wholly owned subsidiary and another 3.4 GW under joint ventures. The company is targeting 60 GW of renewable energy capacity by FY32. However, Nomura has flagged transmission availability as a key risk, warning that connectivity constraints could delay project commissioning and limit capacity additions compared with the company’s guidance.

The broader investment trend suggests that India’s renewable energy expansion is entering a more execution-sensitive phase. As storage becomes integral to power procurement, access to transmission infrastructure, battery costs and commissioning schedules are likely to influence developers’ earnings visibility and capital efficiency. For investors, the distinction between announced capacity and operational assets remains critical, particularly as renewable developers compete to deliver dependable electricity rather than generation capacity alone.
